Meta.Title: DeepFace Performance
Meta.Introduction: Simulation that gradually increases load on a DeepFace web service, to analyze performance, error rate and latency during different loads.
Meta.Description: Simulates 10 web clients, each representing a Neuron accessing a single DeepFace web service, during 1 minute. Web clients requests face vectorization with a frequency that is gradually increased over time. During the simulation, performance metrics are sampled.
Meta.Preparation:
Face Database ----------------
For the simulation to work, a face image database needs to be used. Any face image database can be used, as long as it is based on a set of images stored in a folder structure, with a common root folder. During the setup of the simulation, the path to the root folder of the face image database has to be entered. For this simlation the face database [`celebahq`](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/lamsimon/celebahq) has been used. It consists of JPG images of celebrities each one around 100 kB in size, and 1024x1024 pixels.
Reverse Proxy ----------------
The [TAG Neuron](https://lab.tagroot.io/Broker.md) or the [IoT Gateway](https://waher.se/IoTGateway/Index.md) web server used to define the reverse proxy that redirects requests to the local DeepFace has to be setup. This is done in the `Gateway.config` file, or in the `GatewayConfig` Data Source, under the `WebServer` node. The following XML can be pasted into the `WebServer` node using the [Simple IoT Client](https://waher.se/IoTGateway/SimpleIoTClient.md), to add the reverse proxy node. You might have to change the remote parameters, in case the Docker component uses other values. The Neuron or Gateway needs to be restarted afterward, for the changes to take effect.
```xml <createNewNode xmlns="urn:nf:iot:concentrator:1.0" type="Waher.Service.IoTBroker.Sources.GatewayConfig.ProxyResource" id="WebServer" src="GatewayConfig"> <x xmlns="jabber:x:data" type="submit"> <field var="LocalResource"> <value>/DeepFace</value> </field> <field var="RemoteDomain"> <value>192.168.100.10</value> </field> <field var="RemoteFolder"> <value>/</value> </field> <field var="RemotePort"> <value>5000</value> </field> <field var="Encrypted"> <value>false</value> </field> <field var="UseSession"> <value>true</value> </field> <field var="TimeoutMs"> <value>30000</value> </field> <field var="Privilege"> <value></value> </field> </x> </createNewNode> ```
DeepFace -----------
DeepFace runs in a container environment protected by a Neuron that faces the Internet. It has a reverse proxy, that forwards requests to the local DeepFace web service, and forwards any reponses back to the web client.
During initial setup of the simulation, the URL to the Reverse Proxy that redirects requests to the DeepFace Web Service has to be entered.
```dot:Connected Entities digraph G { rankdir=LR
subgraph cluster_0 { style=filled; color=lightgrey; node [style=filled,color=white]; label = "Laptop in Chile"; Simulator [label="Simulator\nComSim"] }
subgraph cluster_1 { style=filled; color=lightgrey; node [style=filled,color=white]; label = "VM in Azure in Western Europe"; Neuron [label="Neuron\nReverse Proxy"] DeepFace [label="DeepFace\nin Docker container"] }
Simulator -> Neuron [label="HTTP/2.0 GET/POST"] Neuron -> DeepFace [label="HTTP/2.0 GET/POST"] DeepFace -> Neuron [label="HTTP/2.0 Response"] Neuron -> Simulator [label="HTTP/2.0 Response"] } ```
Performance Counters ------------------------
For this simulation to work, the `Performance.ws` Web Service script available in the [Examples](https://github.com/Trust-Anchor-Group/ComSim/tree/master/Examples) folder in the [ComSim](https://github.com/Trust-Anchor-Group/ComSim) project, needs to be copied to Neuron hosting the reverse proxy and DeepFace, for example to the `Reports/Performance.ws` file resource. When the simulatio starts, a URL to the web service must be entered.
For readability, then web service script contais the following script:
{ "cpuPercent":PerformanceCounterValue("Processor","_Total","% Processor Time"), "networkBytesPerSec":PerformanceCounterValue("Network Interface","Microsoft Hyper-V Network Adapter","Bytes Total/sec"), "memoryMBytesFree":PerformanceCounterValue("Memory","Available MBytes") }

StochasticEvent.Description: Raised when the DeepFace API endpoint is tested.
Raised when a face is vectorized using the DeepFace API.

EventHandler.Description: Server performance is measured regularly during the simulation, and shown in the final report.

Activity.Description: Sends an HTTP GET request to the DeepFace API endpoint, to check that the web service is up and running.
Selects a random face from the face database, and sends it in a HTTP POST request to the DeepFace API endpoint, requesting it to vectorize the face in the image.
This activity measures server performance, by calling a web service and reporting the measured values in the returning JSON object back to the simulator.
